topic: Durable Execution for AI Agents: Production Patterns Guide 2026

key_points: OpenAI shows why long-running model tasks time out in synchronous flows and presents `background=true` as a production-safe pattern.
Background mode stores response payloads for roughly 10 minutes to support polling, which can conflict with zero-data-retention requirements.
LangGraph documents checkpointing as a first-class production primitive, saving graph state automatically after each node execution.
It recommends thread-based persistence for long-running multi-turn conversations and notes widespread production checkpoint adoption.
Temporal positions durability and transparent retry/failure handling as core for long-running AI agents.
The narrative emphasizes workflow-level resumability as foundational for production-grade agent systems rather than one-off scripts.
This guide frames durable execution as a production baseline and combines checkpointers, retry policies, and state persistence across Temporal, LangGraph, and event-driven workflow platforms.
It highlights idempotency, resumable SSE/stream restart, and human-in-the-loop pause points to reduce silent side-effect drift.
The piece argues most agent failures stem from missing engineering primitives (checkpointing and durable retries) rather than only model quality.
It compares infrastructure runtimes and points to tradeoffs by task duration, side-effect severity, and recovery cost.

stats.fact: In production LLM workflows, a majority of teams are planning AI agent adoption but far fewer have shipped it, creating a classic deployability gap.
OpenAI background execution persists response data for about 10 minutes to support polling, but this breaks ZDR compatibility for the stored response payload.
LangGraph's guidance says production systems commonly use checkpointing to avoid replay loss and keep agent state recoverable across failures.
A 2026 developer survey snapshot notes daily AI-agent usage in work increased from 14% in 2025 to 37% in 2026 in the Stack Overflow pulse sample.
Stripe documents idempotency behavior where retries return the same result for the same key, including preserving 500-style errors, which directly maps to side-effect safety for agent retries.

angles: Treat durability as a contract, not a feature: every externalized side-effect must be replay-safe.
Use a two-layer pattern: agent framework state in checkpoints plus workflow engine durability for process guarantees.
Separate long-running compute from sensitive side effects with async orchestration and explicit human approvals.
Choose the right durability layer by workload profile: low-latency tool bursts, long-running research loops, and multi-agent handoffs need different checkpoint granularity.
